blocks.text: When the rain rolls in off the Tasman and the flags come down at Bondi, I don't head home — I move the day indoors. So what is there to do in Bondi Beach on a rainy day? Plenty. Between the Pavilion's galleries, a long lunch above the pool, café-hopping and the undercover world of Bondi Junction, a wet day here is often one of my favourites. Here are the seven I keep coming back to.
1. Bondi Pavilion — art, theatre and pottery under one roof

The restored Bondi Pavilion is the first place I send anyone caught in a downpour. Right on the promenade, this heritage building reopened in 2022 after a major restoration and now holds an art gallery, a theatre, music studios, a pottery studio and the Bondi Story Room. Programming rotates constantly, so check the Waverley Council Pavilion page for what's on — and the galleries are free to wander.
Grab a window seat upstairs between showers — you get the whole sweep of the beach and the surf turning moody and grey, a better view than any blue-sky day.
2. A long lunch at Icebergs, dry above a churning sea

There's no better place to watch a storm than the dining room and bar at [Icebergs](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/icebergs-dining-room-and-bar), on the top level of 1 Notts Avenue above the famous ocean pool. It's a celebrated Italian restaurant with floor-to-ceiling views, and on a wild day the waves crashing over the pool below are pure theatre. Check idrb.com for current menus, prices and reservations.
3. Café-hopping through North Bondi

Rain is the perfect excuse to slow down over coffee, and Bondi's café scene is genuinely world-class — if you want to plan a proper crawl, our full guide to [Bondi's best cafés and coffee](/bondi-eat-and-drink/best-cafes-bondi-beach) maps out where to go. I'll linger over eggs and a flat white at [Porch & Parlour](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/porch-and-parlour) on Ramsgate Avenue, or grab a corner at [Speedos Café](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/speedos-cafe) up the North Bondi end and watch the wet promenade go by.

blocks.title: Cafés get cosy-busy when it rains
blocks.text: Everyone has the same idea on a wet Sunday, so the popular spots fill fast mid-morning. Go early, or wait out the peak under the Pavilion arches.
4. A wellness reset — massage, sauna or a yoga class

A grey day is tailor-made for self-care. Bondi is full of day spas, massage studios and yoga schools where you can book a treatment or drop into a class while the rain empties the streets. Rather than name prices that change, find a studio near your accommodation and book directly.
5. Read, borrow or just shelter at Waverley Library

One of Bondi's best rainy-day secrets is free: Waverley Library at the Ron Lander Centre in Bondi Junction. It's a lovely public library with quiet reading nooks, a big children's section, newspapers and free Wi-Fi — a no-pressure spot for families or anyone who wants to dry off with a book. Check the Waverley Council library page for current opening hours, which vary on weekends.
6. Lose an afternoon in a bookshop-café at Gertrude & Alice

When I want to disappear from the weather entirely, I head to [Gertrude & Alice](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/gertrude-and-alice-cafe-bookstore) on Hall Street — a much-loved Bondi bookshop-café stacked floor to ceiling with new and secondhand books, with communal tables, good coffee and cake. Pull something off the shelf, order a chai and settle in. Check gertrudeandalice.com.au for opening hours and events.

blocks.title: Planning on the Bondi Junction cinema?
blocks.text: Event Cinemas Bondi Junction is closed while Westfield's Level 6 entertainment precinct is rebuilt, with a reopening flagged for later in 2026 — check the Event Cinemas page before counting on a film there.
7. Retail therapy, all undercover

When you just want to stay bone dry for hours, Westfield Bondi Junction is the answer — hundreds of shops, food courts and cafés under one roof with the transport interchange right there. It's a short bus ride from the sand on the 333 or 380, so you can duck out the moment the sky clears.
The 333 and 380 buses link Bondi Beach straight to the Bondi Junction interchange, so you can chain the library, the shops and a long lunch into one dry afternoon.

items.q: What is there to do in Bondi Beach when it rains?
items.a: The Bondi Pavilion galleries and theatre, a long lunch at Icebergs, café-hopping through North Bondi, a spa or yoga session, Waverley Library, a browse at Gertrude & Alice, and undercover shopping at Westfield.

items.q: Is there anything free to do in Bondi on a rainy day?
items.a: Yes — wandering the Bondi Pavilion's art gallery and public spaces is free, and Waverley Library in Bondi Junction is a free place to read, use the Wi-Fi or entertain the kids.

items.q: What can families do with kids in Bondi when it's wet?
items.a: Waverley Library has a big children's section and quiet corners, and the Bondi Pavilion often runs family workshops and has the interactive Bondi Story Room.

items.q: Do I need to book anything in advance?
items.a: For a table at Icebergs or a spa treatment, yes — book through their websites and confirm prices there. The Pavilion, library and Gertrude & Alice are all walk-in.

blocks.text: So don't write off a rainy day in Bondi. Some of my best afternoons started with the flags coming down — a gallery, a long lunch and a good book. Rain or shine, this corner of Sydney always has somewhere dry to be.
